$comment: The smithing table is vanilla's cube: an iron plate on top, tongs on its front and back, a hammer painted on its two sides. The scene turns to the player. At the station the block is swapped for body (the same cube whose one side shows no painted hammer: that face is made of strips of the same side texture, the hammer's strip taken from the plain planks beside it) and the real hammer (smithing_hammer, anchored at the end of its grip) hangs where the painting was; SmithingTableBehavior turns body so that side is the scene's right (x 0) when the player came to the table's front or back, its front (z 0) when to a side, and takes the hammer off its hook onto the plate during the flight, and back on leaving. On the plate, as in vanilla's screen from left to right as the camera sees it: template, base (the gear), addition (the material), in a row on the near half. The result hovers low over the plate at the far left; the hammer lies on its side along the far edge, grip on the right. A click on the hammer or on the result strikes: the hammer swings down onto the base, the template and the material are pressed onto it, sparks fly, and the result is taken (the vanilla click on the result slot, at the blow). choice_N, left of the result off the table's edge in two rows, are the other things the pieces make when Polymorph lets the player choose (RecipeChoice; a click makes one the result), hidden otherwise. The camera stands above the near edge looking down at about 55 degrees, as at the crafting table. The hotbar stays where the HUD has it and takes clicks; over it rows of the other stacks the smithing table takes. forged shows what was made rising off the gear for a moment after the blow.
